newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Photo's profit rises on cost-cutting efforts.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Photo's profit rises on cost-cutting efforts.

text.p: Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd's profits rose in the interim period, helped mainly by its cost reduction efforts and the yen's fall against the dollar.

Japan's largest photo film maker said on Friday that it posted 401 billion yen ($3.61 billion) in sales in the first half of the 1996/97 business year, up 1.4 percent from a year earlier. Parent current profits were up five percent to 589.6 billion yen ($5.31 billion).
Current profit is pre-tax profit, including losses and gains on investments.
"The biggest reason for the rise in profits was our efforts to cut costs," said a Fuji Photo spokesman.
He said the company reduced marketing costs and other operational costs in the April-September period by 5.5 percent from a year earlier to 94.8 billion yen ($854 million).

The yen's decline against the dollar also helped. A weaker yen helps to boost yen-denominated income and overseas sales. The downside for the company was that competition continued to be severe in both the domestic and overseas markets, Fuji Photo said in a statement.
It said the introduction in April of cameras based on new advanced photo system (APS) technology contributed to the camera market's revival.
The arrival of the product boosted sales of colour film, disposable cameras and small film-development laboratories.
The company spokesman said a big factor that could affect the company's second-half earnings is foreign exchange rates.
For the full year, Fuji Photo forecasts sales to total 818 billion yen ($7.36 billion) and parent current profits to reach 120 billion yen ($1.08 billion).
Looking forward, a bitter Japan-U.S. trade dispute over Japan's photo film market could negatively affect the company's business.
Last year, Eastman Kodak Co filed a petition with the U.S. Trade Representative saying that Fuji Photo's dominance in the Japanese photo market is maintained by its restrictive business practices.
The U.S. and Japanese governments began talks on the issue under the dispute settlement procedures of the World Trade Organisation in July. ($1=111 yen)
